---
title: "Within-group residual correlation"
---

# Within-group residual correlation

> **Maturity: experimental** ([#1081](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1081)).

Repeated measurements of one trial arm are not independent draws. When a
model-based meta-analysis (MBMA) fits arm means visit by visit, the residuals of
one arm share whatever the structural model leaves out of that arm, and scoring
them as independent overstates how much the data know. A `correlation` line in
`[error_model]` lets the residuals of the rows of one group correlate:

```
[parameters]
  theta RHO(0.3, -0.2, 0.95)        # an ordinary theta: bounds, FIX, priors and SE apply
  sigma ADD_ERR ~ 1.0 (variance) FIX

[error_model]
  DV ~ additive(ADD_ERR) weight = WPSE
  correlation cs(RHO) by ARM         # or ar1(RHO), car1(RHO)
```

## What it means

Rows of one subject (`ID`) with the same value of the `by` column form one
**residual block**. Within a block the residual covariance is

```
R_jk = C_jk(ρ) · Σ_s c_j,s c_k,s σ_s²
```

where `c` are the row's own sigma loadings — the same ones its variance uses, so
they carry the [`weight =`](error-model.qmd#residual-weighting-weight-...) scaling and
any [custom magnitude](error-model.qmd#time-varying-covariate-dependent-magnitude).
For a weighted additive endpoint that is `R = σ² · W C W` with `W = diag(weight)`:
the diagonal is exactly the variance the row has without the line, and the
correlation sits off it. Rows in different blocks, or of different subjects, are
independent; a block never spans two subjects.

For one arm with visits at `t = 0, 2, 12`:

```
cs:   C = [[1, ρ, ρ],      ar1:  C = [[1,  ρ,  ρ²],    car1:  C = [[1,   ρ²,  ρ¹²],
           [ρ, 1, ρ],                 [ρ,  1,  ρ ],                [ρ²,  1,   ρ¹⁰],
           [ρ, ρ, 1]]                 [ρ², ρ,  1 ]]                [ρ¹², ρ¹⁰, 1  ]]
```

- `cs` — **compound symmetry** (nlme's `corCompSymm`): every two rows of a block
  correlate by `ρ`.
- `ar1` — **first-order autoregressive** (nlme's `corAR1`): rows `a` positions
  apart in the block's **time order** correlate by `ρ^a`, whatever the time
  between them. The order is the data's `TIME`, not the row order of the file.
- `car1` — **continuous-time first-order autoregressive** (nlme's `corCAR1`): rows
  at times `t_a` and `t_b` correlate by `ρ^|t_a − t_b|`, so the correlation decays
  with the time between them, in the units of the data's `TIME`. `ρ` is the
  correlation of two rows one time unit apart. On a regular visit grid one unit
  apart, `car1` is `ar1`; on irregular visits they differ.

With a combined error, both the proportional and the additive component
correlate by the same `C`: `R_jk = C_jk (f_j f_k σ_p² + w_j w_k σ_a²)`.

## Syntax and rules

```
correlation <structure>(THETA) by COLUMN
correlation <structure>(THETA) by (COLUMN1, COLUMN2)
```

- `<structure>` is `cs`, `ar1` or `car1`. At most one `correlation` line per model.
- The argument is a θ declared in `[parameters]`, and **only** the `correlation`
  line may read it: a θ that also appears in a model expression is refused, since
  its gradient would then split across two channels.
- `by` names one or more data columns; their combined value names the block,
  within `ID`. A row whose `by` value is missing is in no block. The columns are
  required data columns, like any covariate the model reads. On a model with
  nested levels, `by` may name one level instead
  ([below](#with-kappa-and-nested-levels)).
- `ρ` `FIX`ed at `0` drops the line, as a `FIX` zero `block_sigma` off-diagonal
  is dropped: the model is then the independent one, bit for bit. A free `ρ`
  starting at 0 keeps the line.

Admissible values are checked against the data before the fit
(`E_RESIDUAL_CORRELATION_RANGE`):

| Structure | `ρ` must lie in | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `cs` | `(−1/(n_max − 1), 1)`, `n_max` the largest block | compound symmetry over `n` rows is a valid covariance only there |
| `ar1` | `(−1, 1)` | |
| `car1` | `[0, 1)` | `ρ^Δt` is undefined for a negative `ρ` and a non-integer `Δt`; for a negative correlation between consecutive rows use `ar1` |
| any, `ρ` free | also within ±0.995 | as `|ρ| → 1` the rows of a block become collinear and `R` numerically singular |

A free `ρ` is checked on its θ **bounds**, a `FIX`ed one on its value, so `FIX`
lifts the ±0.995 rail. An unbounded θ keeps the default upper bound of `1e9`
and is refused: bound it. A `car1` θ with a lower bound of 0 is estimated on the
log scale, like any θ bounded below by 0, so it stays positive. Two rows of one
block at the same `TIME` are refused under `ar1`, where they have no order, and
under `car1`, where they correlate by `ρ⁰ = 1` and make `R` singular
(`E_RESIDUAL_CORRELATION_TIES`). Under both, a block may not span a stacked reset
occasion (an `EVID=3/4` record that restarts `TIME`): its rows' times are then on
two clocks, so their order and the time between them are undefined. Add the
occasion column to `by`, or use `cs` (`E_RESIDUAL_CORRELATION_RESET`). A line under
which every block is a single row couples nothing; `ρ` is then not in the
likelihood and ferx says so (`W_RESIDUAL_CORRELATION_INERT`).

`simulate()` refuses the same inputs with the same codes (#1976): `ρ` is checked
on the value it draws at, as a `FIX`ed one is at fit time (so the ±0.995 rail
does not apply), and the `TIES` and `RESET` data checks run on the population it
is handed.

## Scope

The line is fitted by `method = foce` and `focei` only. Refused, each with
`E_RESIDUAL_CORRELATION_SCOPE` naming the method or feature:

- every other method (`saem`, `imp`, `impmap`, `laplace`, `vi`, `gn`, `bayes`,
  and a chain that passes through one), and `n_agq > 1`;
- `bloq_method = m3`, FREM, time-to-event / binary / categorical / Markov
  endpoints, `[mixture]`, and SDE (`[diffusion]`) models.

The parser refuses it with a per-CMT or covariate-selected (`if … else`) error
model, with `iiv_on_ruv`, and next to a `block_sigma`, which is a different
residual correlation (between sigmas of one record, or of paired records).

Inter-occasion random effects (`kappa`) and nested levels are supported, with
the one refusal [below](#with-kappa-and-nested-levels).

## With kappa and nested levels

A model with `kappa`, at one level (`iov_column`, or a single `level`) or at
nested levels, fits the line by FOCE and FOCEI (#1082). The marginal
linearizes over every random effect of the subject, so `R̃ = H Σ_b Hᵀ + R`
holds each level's block of `Σ_b` and the line's dense `R`.

**Naming a level in `by`.** On a model with nested levels, `by ARM` naming the
level `ARM` groups the rows by that level's groups, nested by key: arm 1 of
study 1 and arm 1 of study 2 are two blocks, as they are two groups of the
level. A data column groups by its value within `ID`, which would merge them.
Where the two readings could differ, the line is refused with
`E_RESIDUAL_CORRELATION_GROUPING_AMBIGUOUS`, which says what to write:

| `by` | Reads |
|---|---|
| a level's name (`by ARM`) | that level's groups |
| a column no level reads (`by ARMID`) | the column within `ID`, as without levels |
| the column of the first level, whose parent is `ID` | the column; both readings agree |
| a level inside a list (`by (STUDY, ARM)`) | refused: write `by ARM` |
| a level's name that is also a different data column | refused: rename one |
| the column of a nested level under another name | refused: write the level's name |

**`cs` and a kappa at the same grouping are refused.** A kappa gives the rows
of each of its groups one shared random effect, which is the correlation `cs`
estimates (see [Choosing a structure](#choosing-a-structure)). So `cs` whose
blocks group the observation rows exactly as a kappa-carrying level does is
refused with `E_RESIDUAL_CORRELATION_CONFOUNDED_KAPPA`, whatever the kappa's
form. The blocks are compared as partitions in every subject, so `cs by ARMID`
next to `kappa … at ARM` is caught too. `ar1` and `car1` are never refused, and
neither is `cs` over a grouping no kappa is at.

When the blocks match a kappa-carrying level's groups in **some** subjects but
not all, the model is identified, from the subjects where they differ, and fits.
ferx says how many matched, with
`W_RESIDUAL_CORRELATION_PARTLY_CONFOUNDED_KAPPA`, since ρ and the kappa variance
are then separated by the other subjects alone. `cs by STUDY` next to a kappa at
`ARM` is the usual case: the two coincide in every subject whose studies each
have one arm. A `by` column with a typo that splits one group would otherwise
switch the refusal off without a word. A subject where the two agree only
trivially (one observation, or every row its own block) couples no rows under
`cs` and counts on neither side.

**Validation.** ferx scores NONMEM's own `exact3` optimum
(`nonmem_anchor/nested_levels_3_ar1/`, sponsor → study → arm, `ARM` repeating
across studies) with `ar1` at ρ = 0.5 and −0.4, `car1` at 0.6 and a ρ = 0
control, NONMEM writing the arm's residuals through `L2` and a hand-built
Cholesky factor: the worst OFV difference is 5.7e-8 and the worst EBE
difference 1.7e-7 (Linux).

## With a profiled level block

A `profile`d θ level block ([Parameters](parameters.qmd)) fits next to the line
(#2110), with kappas and nested levels. The profile solve does not build a
covariance of its own: its Newton matrix `2XᵀR̃⁻¹X` and its gradient are
differences of the subject objective, so `R̃` is the one the objective scores,
dense `R` included. `ρ` is a structural θ and stays in the outer search.

The line's refusals come before the profile's, so `cs` over a kappa-carrying
level is still `E_RESIDUAL_CORRELATION_CONFOUNDED_KAPPA`. Every
`covariance_method` works next to the line (#2108): `rsr` scores `S` and
re-profiles `R` through the line's dense `R̃`.

**Validation.** On ferx-r's `mbma_placebo` example with
`correlation car1(RHO) by OCC` next to the arm kappa, and again with `ar1`, the
profiled fit and the unprofiled fit started at its optimum agree. The car1
profiled fit reaches OFV 89.451279 (the unprofiled fit's optimum), the unprofiled
restart gains 7.5e-7, the structural θ move by at most 2.5e-4 relative and ρ by
2.8e-6, and the standard errors of the structural θ and ρ agree to 0.45% (Linux).
On `nested_levels_3` (sponsor → study → arm) with a profiled per-study
`PLACEBO[STUDYID]` block and `ar1(RHO) by ARM`, the OFV agrees to 2e-8, the
unprofiled restart moves no estimate, and the standard errors agree to 0.52%. At ρ = 0 the profiled
fit is the fit without the line to a few ULP, the same gap the objective itself
has there, since the line keeps the dense marginal at any ρ.

## Estimation

`ρ` reaches the objective through `R` alone. A subject with a block of two or
more rows takes the exact analytic outer gradient of the dense-`R` objective
(#1960), `∂R/∂ρ` included, under both `method = focei` and `method = foce`, and a
subject whose blocks are all single rows keeps the scalar analytic one (for it
`∂/∂ρ = 0`, correctly). A model that also uses `weight =` takes the exact
analytic outer gradient as well (#2093), with the weight in `R`, and its EBE
search runs on, and reports, the exact inner gradient (#2209). A model with `kappa` (one level or nested) takes the exact analytic
gradient too (#2101): its IOV marginal is the dense-`R` objective over the stacked
`[η, κ]` system, which the adjoint gradient differentiates as it does a model
without `kappa`, on FOCE and FOCEI, and the covariance step takes the exact
analytic R-matrix. Its EBE search runs on the exact gradient of the dense inner
objective. Checked against central differences of the reconverged OFV and of the
gradient, and against the NONMEM anchor above. None of these paths approximates
the objective. The dense gradient's `σ` and
`block_sigma` `ρ` terms are central differences of `R`, exact because `R` is
quadratic in `σ` and linear in that `ρ` (a stencil that straddles the variance
floor declines instead), and the finite-difference paths are only slower.

On the naproxen MBMA below, the default outer tolerances stop BOBYQA about
0.03 OFV short of the optimum along a flat TVEMAX / B_EMAX_FLARE ridge. That is
the optimizer, not the objective — ferx scores NONMEM's optimum at NONMEM's OFV —
and `outer_ftol = 1e-10`, `outer_xtol = 1e-8`, `stagnation_guard = false` reach
it.

## Choosing a structure

- **`cs` and an arm random intercept are the same covariance.** On a weighted
  additive endpoint, `cs` with `ρ ≥ 0` is exactly a `kappa` intercept on the arm,
  loaded by `W`, with variance `ρσ²`, plus a residual of variance `(1 − ρ)σ²`:
  measured equal to 2e-10 in OFV. The two are confounded, not complementary, which
  is why a model may not carry both: `cs` over the groups of a kappa-carrying
  level is refused (`E_RESIDUAL_CORRELATION_CONFOUNDED_KAPPA`), for a
  multiplicative kappa too, whose time course only nearly separates it from
  `cs`. Use `cs` when you want the correlation, and negative values, without
  declaring a random effect; with a kappa at the grouping, use `ar1` or `car1`.
- **`ar1`** is for serial dependence: the correlation decays with the number of
  visits between two rows. On the naproxen data it fits 6 OFV points better than
  `cs` for the same one parameter.
- **`car1`** is serial dependence that decays with elapsed time rather than visit
  count, which is what irregularly spaced MBMA timepoints call for in principle.
  Which of the two fits better is an empirical question: on the naproxen data
  (visits between week 0 and week 13) `ar1` fits 10.9 OFV points better than
  `car1`, for the same one parameter.
- A `factor()` effect on the visit absorbs mean structure, not residual
  dependence; it is not a substitute.

## Diagnostics

The pooled Durbin–Watson statistic and lag-1 correlation (`dw_statistic`,
`iwres_lag1_r`) are taken on each subject's residuals decorrelated by the fitted
`R`, `L⁻¹(y − IPRED)` with `R = L Lᵀ`. Under the model these are independent, so a
value outside `[1.5, 2.5]` reports dependence the line does **not** explain. On the
naproxen data at NONMEM's optima:

| | raw IWRES | decorrelated |
|---|---|---|
| `cs` | 0.99 | 1.43 — warns, with the `ar1` advice |
| `ar1` | 0.94 | 1.69 — silent |

Compound symmetry correlates every two visits of an arm equally, and what is left
is the decay with distance that `ar1` carries. Under `car1` a warning names `ar1`
as the alternative that decays with the visit order instead of the time. The `IWRES` column is unchanged
(per-row standardised).

A `by` column that no model expression reads is a required data column but is not
listed in the "used in model expressions but not declared in `[covariates]`"
warning: its type changes nothing.

## Simulation

`simulate()` and the NPDE reference simulation draw the residual vector of a
subject from the same `R`, reading the blocks from the `by` columns of the data
they are given.

## Comparison with NONMEM

NONMEM has no residual-correlation record, so the anchor spells the same `R` by
hand: `L2 = ARM` makes `EPS(1..5)` one shared vector per arm, and each visit
mixes them through the closed-form Cholesky factor of `C(ρ)`, with `ρ = THETA(8)`.
On the naproxen MBMA (Boucher & Bennetts 2018: 18 studies, 36 arms, 2–5 visits
per arm at irregular times), at fixed parameters:

| Probe | NONMEM 7.6.0 OBJ | ferx | |Δ| |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cs`, ρ = 0 | −173.507683912 | −173.507683911 | 1.1e-9 |
| `cs`, ρ = 0.5 | −198.095096125 | −198.095096126 | 8.1e-10 |
| `cs`, ρ = −0.2 | −109.372389054 | −109.372389053 | 1.6e-9 |
| `ar1`, ρ = 0.5 | −202.052628694 | −202.052628695 | 9.7e-10 |
| `ar1`, ρ = −0.4 | −121.386775570 | −121.386775567 | 2.8e-9 |
| `car1`, ρ = 0.8 | −181.691383297 | −181.691383296 | 1.2e-9 |
| `car1`, ρ = 0.3 | −176.591803241 | −176.591803240 | 1.0e-9 |

For `car1` the NONMEM factor reads each arm's visit times from the data,
`L_jk = ρ^(t_j − t_k) · √(1 − ρ^(2(t_k − t_(k−1))))`.

With a combined error (`combined(PROP_ERR, ADD_ERR) weight = WPSE`, proportional SD
0.03), where `R` depends on the prediction and FOCEI's inner search sees the
correlation's `∂R/∂f`, six probes (`cs` ρ = 0, 0.5; `ar1` ρ = −0.4, 0.5; `car1`
ρ = 0.3, 0.8) agree with NONMEM's `METHOD=1 INTER` to 6.2e-8 at worst.

Estimated, every θ and ω free (`METHOD=1`, `$COV MATRIX=R`); ferx on Linux aarch64, the
reference platform for fit numbers:

| | NONMEM OBJ | NONMEM ρ̂ (SE) | ferx OBJ | ferx ρ̂ (SE) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cs` | −199.734575 | 0.509450 (0.077592) | −199.734563 | 0.509389 (0.077557) |
| `ar1` | −205.932728 | 0.597282 (0.063339) | −205.932727 | 0.597276 (0.063273) |
| `car1` | −195.027166 | 0.813375 (0.037249) | −195.027165 | 0.813378 (0.037137) |

against −173.508 for independent residuals: 26, 32 and 22 OFV points for one
parameter. `car1`'s ρ̂ is per week, the data's `TIME` unit, started at 0.5 with a
lower bound of 0. The control streams, results and an independent closed-form oracle are
in `nonmem_anchor/residual_correlation/`; the tests are
`tests/residual_correlation_nonmem_anchor.rs`.
